subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Primary and Secondary Amenorrhoea and Turner Syndrome

steps.tx: No menstruation by fifteen years with secondary characters, or thirteen without, defines **primary amenorrhoea**. Causes divide by breast development and uterus presence into a memorable grid. Most have a specific, often treatable diagnosis. Breasts present with no uterus points to MRKH or androgen insensitivity; breasts absent splits ovarian from central causes.
steps.say: Primary amenorrhoea is no menstruation by fifteen with secondary characters.

steps.tx: Cessation of periods for three to six months after established cycles is **secondary amenorrhoea**. Pregnancy is always excluded first, then thyroid, prolactin and PCOS dominate causes. Hypothalamic suppression from weight and stress is common. Three months is the cut off after previously regular cycles, six months after irregular ones.
steps.say: Secondary amenorrhoea excludes pregnancy first, then thyroid, prolactin and PCOS.

steps.tx: Bleeding after progestogen in an oestrogen primed woman proves a patent outflow and some oestrogen, the **progesterone challenge test**. No bleed means low oestrogen or outflow block, separated by an oestrogen plus progestogen cycle. It is now largely replaced by direct hormone panels.
steps.say: The progesterone challenge test proves outflow patency and oestrogen presence by bleeding.

steps.tx: Streak ovaries from a missing X chromosome causing short stature and amenorrhoea form **Turner syndrome**. Forty five X is the classic karyotype, with mosaics milder. Oestrogen replacement induces puberty and protects bone and heart. Cardiac echo at diagnosis looks for coarctation and bicuspid aortic valve, found in about a third.
steps.say: Turner syndrome with forty five X causes short stature and streak ovaries.

steps.tx: Webbed neck, wide carrying angle and coarctation accompany the Turner phenotype as **somatic features**. Cardiac screening is lifelong because aortic dilatation can dissect. Growth hormone in childhood adds adult height. Wide spaced nipples and a short fourth metacarpal add to the examination list candidates recite.
steps.say: Turner somatic features need lifelong cardiac screening for aortic dilatation.

steps.tx: Hypergonadotropic failure with high FSH separates ovarian causes from hypothalamic low FSH patterns, termed **gonadotropin sorting**. One blood test halves the differential instantly. It is the pivotal investigation in amenorrhoea. An FSH above 25 international units per litre on two samples points firmly to ovarian insufficiency.
steps.say: Gonadotropin sorting by FSH halves the amenorrhoea differential instantly.

steps.tx: A young woman with ovarian failure may still ovulate on a good month. **POI fluctuation** means hormone levels and follicle activity swing unpredictably in premature ovarian insufficiency, especially early in its course. One normal FSH reading can therefore falsely reassure. Repeat testing and honest counselling hold both truths together: reserve is severely reduced, yet spontaneous pregnancy occasionally happens and contraception is still needed when pregnancy is not wanted.
steps.say: Hormones fluctuate in premature ovarian insufficiency, so one normal FSH can falsely reassure. Reserve is low, yet occasional ovulation still occurs.

vis.alt: Image showing fluctuating hormone activity in premature ovarian insufficiency.
vis.caption: Hormone levels are shown rising and falling unpredictably in premature ovarian insufficiency. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Hormones that refuse to sit still tell a different story from hormones that have simply failed. In **premature ovarian insufficiency**, FSH and oestradiol fluctuate month to month because residual follicles fire unpredictably before the ovary finally quiets. One reassuring oestradiol value therefore never excludes the diagnosis. This intermittency explains occasional spontaneous ovulation and pregnancy years after presentation, and it is why counselling avoids promising either fertility or its permanent loss.
steps.say: In premature ovarian insufficiency, FSH and oestradiol fluctuate as residual follicles fire unpredictably. One normal value never excludes the diagnosis.

vis.alt: Endocrine chart showing fluctuating serum FSH and oestradiol levels in premature ovarian insufficiency.
vis.caption: FSH and oestradiol lines swing month to month as residual ovarian activity comes and goes. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Premature ovarian insufficiency before forty affects one percent and may fluctuate, unlike menopause, as **POI fluctuation**. Occasional ovulation and even pregnancy occur in five to ten percent. Bone and cardiovascular protection need oestrogen to fifty one. Oestrogen is continued until the average menopause age, about 51, then reviewed like ordinary hormone therapy.
steps.say: Premature ovarian insufficiency fluctuates, with occasional ovulation unlike menopause.

steps.tx: Absent breast development with absent uterus points to gonadal agenesis variants needing **karyotype first**. Swyer syndrome with forty six XY streak gonads carries gonadoblastoma risk. Gonadectomy follows diagnosis in Y bearing dysgenesis. Swyer gonads are streaks that can turn malignant early, so removal follows diagnosis rather than waiting for puberty.
steps.say: Karyotype first in absent breasts and uterus because Y bearing dysgenesis risks gonadoblastoma.

steps.tx: Outflow causes with normal hormones include imperforate hymen, septum and MRKH, grouped as **Mullerian outflow causes**. Examination and imaging, not bloods, diagnose them. Each has a distinct surgical remedy covered earlier. A transverse vaginal septum traps blood higher than an imperforate hymen, and the perineum looks normal between them.
steps.say: Mullerian outflow causes have normal hormones and imaging diagnoses.
